notes:
User is planning their week and uses Todoist for task management, preferring it after comparing it with Trello. They were interested in Todoist’s Google Calendar integration, but it is unknown whether they enabled it. Todoist fits their current routine.

Routine: gym at 7:00 PM every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday. Suggested Todoist setup: one recurring task at 7:00 PM on M/W/F, ideally with a reminder around 6:00 PM. Do not use “every 2 days,” because it would include unwanted days. During the current meeting-planning conversation, the user said they need to be at the gym by 6:00 PM on this particular Tuesday, so account for that constraint; this may be a temporary schedule variation.

User manages multiple simultaneous projects and wants help prioritizing. Suggested organization: one project per major initiative; consistent labels/filters; priorities, sections, subtasks, templates, and regular reviews. Be careful with Todoist terminology and current capabilities: standard Todoist has four priority levels, not custom priorities 1–4. Verify features such as task dependencies, custom views, or specialized workflows before claiming they are native or included in the user’s plan.

User wants to use Todoist to track goal progress. Todoist can support this indirectly through recurring tasks, completed-task counts/history, Karma/productivity trends, filters, and saved views. Do not claim native SMART goals, goal metrics, progress bars, forecasts, goal notifications/reflections, or project-level goal tracking without checking current documentation/plan availability. A practical approach is to represent a goal as a project, use measurable recurring tasks and milestones, and define success manually.

Current scheduling plan:
- Potential-client meeting tentatively planned for Tuesday at 2:00 PM.
- User wants to finish before a 6:00 PM gym commitment, leaving several hours of buffer.
- Tuesday/Thursday were selected because the user is flexible and avoids M/W/F gym days.
- Meeting duration and purpose/client availability have not been definitively established, though 60 minutes or less was suggested for an introductory meeting.
- The user will share necessary files through Google Drive: create a clearly named folder, organize files, set appropriate permissions, test access, and email the client a link with a brief explanatory note.
- The user plans to send the file link before the meeting and asked whether to confirm logistics; the recommendation was yes. The email should include the meeting date, exact time, expected duration if known, meeting format/location or call link if applicable, purpose, materials shared, and requested review/action. Do not imply the Tuesday date is finalized if confirmation has not occurred.

Useful email structure:
“Hi [Name], I’ve shared a Google Drive folder with the files for our meeting on [full date] at [time] [and time zone]. You can access them here: [link]. The meeting will last approximately [duration] and will be held via [format/location]. The folder contains [brief contents]; please review [specific materials/action] beforehand. I look forward to discussing [purpose/outcome]. Please let me know if the time no longer works or if you have questions.”
